text: [3:487] Ins.C. § 533 as bar to coverage? Section 533 bars coverage for injury claims arising from the insured's “wilful” (intentional) discrimination against employees (see ¶ 3:105 ff.). But the statute does not bar coverage for conduct that may be wrongful, but that was not intentional or wilful from the standpoint of the insured. [Melugin v. Zurich Canada (1996) 50 CA4th 658, 665, 57 CR2d 781, 785] (1) [3:488] “Disparate treatment” vs. “disparate impact” claims: Thus, while there is no coverage for deliberate discrimination in the workplace (“disparate treatment” cases), there may be coverage for discrimination resulting from only unintentional, negligent conduct (so-called “disparate impact” cases). [Melugin v. Zurich Canada, supra, 50 CA4th at 665, 57 CR2d at 785] “Unlike disparate treatment claims, disparate impact claims are not precluded from coverage under § 533.” [Save Mart Supermarkets v.
